precepts.text: That which I do I allow not; for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I. The real spirit connected to God hates evil, and the conditioned self does it anyway. That duality is the daily fight. Christ said deny yourself: the you doing the denying is what God is dealing with, and the self is the composite of conditioning. Examine your behaviour and ask whether it is the real you or a response to conditioning.
precepts.point: I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations. Whatever the Lord ordained us to be, we will be, and he put talents in us. That is why the Bishop stresses organizing those talents; you cannot bring self-doubt around him. Get the doubt out and let the real you stay and be built up.

note.label: The Image of Dysfunction or the Image of God Which One Are You?

precepts.why:
The foundational question is: am I who I was created to be, or am I what I was conditioned to become? It is not a surface-level question; it is an identity question that deals with the real soul of man and woman. Everything about us, our patterns, our responses, our beliefs, our defenses, has been shaped by one of two forces: creation or conditioning. Creation speaks to design; conditioning speaks to experience. One is intentional, the other reactive. One reflects origin, the image God made; the other reflects adaptation, to slavery, to ghettos, to being taken advantage of, to being unclean, a gang member, a drug addict. That is not who we really are, and most people live somewhere in between without ever telling the two apart.

Paul shows that fight in Romans 7:15: “For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I.” What he ends up doing, the real him does not allow. What his spirit would do, the conditioned self will not follow. And what the real him hates, the righteous part connected to God that hates evil, he does anyway, acting from conditioning and not from what the Lord made him to be. “If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good.” That duality goes on with us every day.

Christ said you must deny yourself. The you that does the denying is the part God is dealing with; the self is the composite of the conditioning you were made into. So examine your own thoughts and behaviors and ask: why am I behaving like this? Is this the real me, or a response to what I have been conditioned to be?

Most of the time when we deal with our people, we are dealing with the mask, the representative, like the man holding up a sign in front of himself. The real soul is buried and scared, hiding under a tarp of trauma, lies, deceit and psychological hang-ups. The greatness buried under self-doubt has not surfaced yet. That is what is meant by the Negro being made in a lab: the real him has not stood up. We have to encourage that real spirit to come forward and be the image God made.

precepts.text: What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet. I would not know what sin is but by the law. I would not know what lust is. By studying the word of God you are able to self-examine. You are able to search and try your ways.
precepts.point: Thou hast made us as the offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people. Looked up in class: offscouring is a rare noun that means physical dirt or refuse cleaned off an object, or a person rejected by society as an outcast. Literal waste, dirt, grime or scum scrubbed off a dirty surface. Social outcast, a person treated as scum, trash, or a pariah by society. Biblical use found in older translations like the King James Bible, such as 1 Corinthians 4:13 and Lamentations 3:45, to describe how lowly or despised the apostles and the people of Jerusalem felt.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

precepts.why:
How do we search and try our ways? Paul shows it: “What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet.” I would not know what sin is, but by the law. I would not know what lust is, except the law told me.

So by studying the word of God, you are able to self-examine. You are able to search and try your ways, by studying and reading the word of God. That is what Paul said, and it is what Jeremiah said: “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.”

Without the law a man has no measure to try himself by; he thinks what he is doing is fine. With the law in front of him, he can see where “We have transgressed and have rebelled”, and why the Lord has not pardoned. The law is the mirror, and the one who reads it is the one who can turn again.

precepts.text: The law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good. In order for us to be the holy people that God destines us to be, we must study the law, we must apply the law. And no, we're not talking about animal sacrifice, cuz Christians get stupid. We're talking about laws of morality, laws of civility, laws of ceremony, laws of diet. That's what's holy.
precepts.point: Having predestinated us: there it go again, before the foundation of the world. Unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself. In whom we, the saints, have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
He chose us “that we should be holy and without blame before him in love”. That is difficult for blacks and Latinos: we have hood tendencies. When the videos go up of the fights on the cruise ships, the twerking on cop cars, the twerking in the restaurant a black man opened with his wife, that is not holy.

So how do we become holy? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” In order for us to be the holy people God destines us to be, we must study the law and we must apply the law.

And no, we are not talking about animal sacrifice, because Christians get stupid. We are talking about laws of morality, laws of civility, laws of ceremony, laws of diet. That is what is holy, and that is how the chosen ones become holy and without blame before him.

precepts.text: For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me: you can only acknowledge sin through the commandments of God. The law says thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart; when you meditate on it you realize, I have the evil spirit toward the brother. The law is the light, like fog lights piercing through the cloud of confusion, and what you see on the other side is yourself in the mirror of the Bible.
precepts.point: And Cain talked with Abel his brother: this is the deception. He acted like his friend, talked with him over a period of time, and lured him out to the field. And when they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him. That is the spirit you are rolling in when you move with that bitter spirit; in that wrath you will slay a brother, or in that bitterness you might betray a brother.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
What is bitterness? It is sin. “For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me.” Taking occasion by the commandment means you can only recognize sin through the commandments of God. How do you know you are in the middle of sin? The law says you shall not hate your brother in your heart, and when you meditate on it you realize, I have an evil spirit toward that brother. The law brings it to the surface.

Sin “deceived me”: you did not know bitterness was a sin, because you were deceived. But the law gives clarity. Like fog lights, it pierces the cloud of confusion. That is why the law is called a light: so you can see through the nonsense your mind was thinking.

Then sin “by it slew me.” When the scripture comes out, you feel cut, because you are no longer deceived and can see clearly. What you see on the other side of the fog is yourself in the mirror of the Bible, realizing how evil you were. Some people do not like the light and love to walk in darkness, saying, do not call that out, that is not me; brothers wearing purple and gold, a ribbon of blue and fringes, who are only blue ribbon Christians. We do not want to be those night walkers.

precepts.text: Raguel had one only daughter, named Sarah, and the angel said: fear not, for she is appointed unto thee from the beginning. From ever since the beginning, that was his wife. The Most High does bring people together. So do not develop bitterness and hatred toward each other over who is talking to whom: be happy for the brother; be happy for the sister. Whoever is for you is for you. That bitterness is going to change you, and it is just a matter of time before you leave the body.
precepts.point: And bringing me into captivity to the law of sin: that is what Satan is trying to do, bring you into the captivity of sin, the captivity of bitterness. O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death? I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord: so then with the mind I myself serve the law of God. Everything starts with your mind; when them evil thoughts come to your mind concerning your brother or your sister, you have to shake it off. Do not play with bitterness, hatred, or envy; when these things try creeping up in you, shake it off.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

precepts.why:
“But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin”. The thoughts warring against your mind are Satan, and one of the ways he brings you into the captivity of bitterness is over who is talking to whom. Brothers stop talking to a brother because of a sister. Two sisters were cool, both liked the same brother, and now they have stopped talking to each other. That is bitterness, and that is fake.

Tobit shows how God brings people together. The angel told Tobias, “to day we shall lodge with Raguel, who is thy cousin; he also hath one only daughter, named Sara; I will speak for her, that she may be given thee for a wife. For to thee doth the right of her appertain, seeing thou only art of her kindred.” And he told him, when he came into the marriage chamber and made the smoke, “the devil shall smell it, and flee away, and never come again any more”, and they should rise up both of them and pray to God.

Then: “fear not, for she is appointed unto thee from the beginning”. From ever since the beginning, that was his wife. The Most High does bring people together. If that brother is for you, he is for you. Whoever is for you is for you.

So do not develop bitterness and hatred toward each other over who is talking to whom. Be happy for the brother; be happy for the sister. You brothers cannot stop talking to each other because of a woman, and brothers who roll like that need to repent. That bitterness is going to change you, and it is just a matter of time before you leave the body. “With the mind I myself serve the law of God”: when those evil thoughts about your brother or sister come, shake them off.

precepts.text: The law is holy and the commandment holy, just and good: applying it is what makes you just.
precepts.point: Kings and celebrities with that status will not repent, because when you are rich you become your own god; the world literally calls them idols. Oprah said on air she does not respect a jealous God, because she is a goddess of this world.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
Manasseh prays, “Thou therefore, O Lord, that art the God of the just, hast not appointed repentance to the just.” Obviously: if you are just, you have nothing to repent from. But what makes you just?

Paul answers it: “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” The law is holy, and the commandment is holy, just and good. When you are applying it, that is what makes you just. That is what makes you good: the law and the commandment.

So the God of the just is the God of those who keep the commandments, “as to Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, which have not sinned against thee.” They kept God’s laws. Repentance was not appointed for them.

“But thou hast appointed repentance unto me that am a sinner.” Manasseh knew he was not just. He had broken the holy, just and good commandment on every count, and his only hope was the repentance the Lord appoints unto sinners.

precepts.text: The law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good. The law is what makes Israel a holy people.
precepts.point: Let the sisters get counsel from sisters. When you do give counsel, it must be what God wants them to hear and beneficial to them, not to your own wants.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
“Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” If the law is holy, and God says you are a holy people, then we are supposed to be a law-abiding people. The laws of God are our constitution, the thing we stand on. That is what makes us holy, what makes us special, what makes us set apart: the laws being applied.

The word of God has no power unless you activate it, and the only way to activate it is to do what it says to do. Other than that it is just pages, just words on a page, just a book. The word is alive and living when you let it live through you by your actions. You become the word, the living example of what it means to be a holy people. That is why the nations say, what a wise and understanding people. They see our actions.

We witness that already at the big events in the big arenas. They say, thousands of black men and nobody smoking weed, no fights breaking out. Then look at what happened in Houston at the rodeo, and how they laughed at us; we are a joke to them. But when we move they ask, how are they so organized, how can they mobilize a few thousand men, put them on the street and file them back in like that, nobody fighting and the place clean? That is the word of God working through us. There is a standard we live by because we are gods on the earth, and it is second nature to us as a nation.

So do not walk in hypocrisy. God gave us something that will make us shine bright and obtain the kingdom. Be that living example to the people.

precepts.text: The law is holy and the commandment holy, just and good: what makes you just, and the just live by faith in Christ.
precepts.point: The just shall live by faith, from Habakkuk; the law is not of faith but the promise predates the law and sacrifice; and Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us, so that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles, the northern kingdom.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
What makes you just, so that you live by faith? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” The law is holy, and the commandment is holy and just and good.

So when you are just, what are you keeping? God's laws. And what will you live by? Faith in Christ. That is what Habakkuk is talking about when he says the just shall live by his faith, and that is what Paul is talking about in Galatians 3:11. The just are those who keep God's commandments, and they shall live by faith.

So Paul is not throwing away the commandments. The law that cannot justify is the law of sacrifice; the commandments are what make a man just, and the just man lives by faith in Christ.

precepts.text: The law is spiritual, but I am carnal, sold under sin. To stop being carnal, keep the law.
precepts.point: The camp is not small any more. A brother making a delivery in another state got recognized by someone outside the truth. If he had been doing wickedness, that is how easily it gets found out.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

precepts.why:
“Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” What is the Spirit you have to walk in so that you never do amiss? “For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.” The law is spiritual. We are carnal, sold under sin. So if we want to stop being carnal and stop sinning, we have to keep the law.

That is what walking in the Spirit means: walking in the ordinances, the laws, the statutes and the commandments of the Lord God. If you are doing these things, you are never going to do amiss.

“For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh”. There is a war within you. The old man always wants to be around, in your business: reading the Bible? You don't need to read the Bible. Let's go rob a house, steal a car, boost cars like you used to, call your man for two birds, go fly some kites. The only way you win this war is by actually reading your Bible and applying what you read.

If you do not read, pray or fast, miss all the new moons and feast days, and show up on the Sabbath just to keep up appearances, you will not be able to fight the lust within your flesh, because you are not walking in the Spirit. The flesh will always be present; it is what you put in you now that fights it. So stay in this book, the spiritual law, and the carnal man is subdued.

precepts.text: Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.
precepts.point: Keep my commandments and live. Whoever does not keep the law will not live.

note.label: My Temple My Choice

precepts.why:
“Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy”. When God says sanctify yourselves and be holy, you have to be applying the law, the statutes and the commandments. The churches do not want you to learn the Old Testament, because they do not want you to be saved. The scripture says choose life, but if you do not know what the law says, how are you going to choose life?

Solomon shows the way to life: “My son, keep my words, and lay up my commandments with thee. Keep my commandments, and live”. If you are not keeping the laws, you are not going to live. So when you keep eating unclean food and are not controlling what you eat, you are sinning.

“And my law as the apple of thine eye.” If somebody tried to poke your eye, you would move fast, like flash, because you do not take chances with something that could blind you. If somebody poked your arm you would not move that fast. The same way you protect your eye, you should protect the law. The moment anything tries to make you go against God’s law, you should move fast. But too many are like a fly drawn to the light that is about to kill it: instead of moving away, they keep going toward it.

The only way to have life is to keep the commandments as the apple of your eye, and that includes the command not to eat garbage and not to overeat. The Most High wants a fit army. You cannot step in the street teaching people discipline when you yourself do not have it.

precepts.text: Sin is the transgression of the law.
precepts.point: Keep my commandments and live. Whoever does not keep the law will not live.

note.label: My Temple My Choice

precepts.why:
If the law is holy and just and good, then what is it to break it? “Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.”

The law of the beasts in Leviticus 11 was given “to make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.” Some animals are clean and some are unclean; it is basic. So eating the unclean, pork, lobster, shrimp, oysters, snails (escargot is just French for snails), crabs, chitlins, pig feet, is transgressing the law, and transgressing the law is sin.

Overeating is sin too. Brothers who are strong in many areas, who left the porn, the smoking and the stealing when they came to the truth, still cannot say, I am not going to overeat any more. There is one area kicking their butt, to the point where they will lie about it: drinking from the brother’s slurpee on the way back from the store, eating the whole house’s bread and saying nah with the crumbs all over the bed. Where there is one sin there are many more; a demon does not walk by itself.

So keeping the holy law means keeping all of it. Gluttony and unclean food are not small things outside the commandments; they are the transgression of the law, and that is sin.

precepts.text: The wages of sin is death.
precepts.point: Keep my commandments and live. Whoever does not keep the law will not live.

note.label: My Temple My Choice

precepts.why:
And what does sin pay? “For the wages of sin is death”. So eating pork is going to kill you. Overeating is going to kill you. Aren’t you supposed to be the temple of God? If you keep eating a certain way, you are destroying yourself, and God will destroy him that destroys the body.

If you do not care about the vehicle the Most High gave you, how will you do the job we are all called here to do? When it is time for missions you cannot go. Brothers over a certain weight class cannot go to camp, and many will fall out of the truth over it: first staying home, then every week a different story, sick, the sniffles, until they find out they love food more than they love the Lord. God forbid something pops off at camp and you become a liability.

As we prepare for the end, get your eating under control. They can starve you for five days, then put you in a room with a Thanksgiving dinner, and you will spill your guts, just as in the Maccabees they tried to make them eat pork. If you cannot control yourself around a slurpee, you will betray this truth for fried chicken.

The law is holy, and keeping it is life; transgressing it is sin, and the wages of sin is death. We warn you because we are trying to save your life. When the high cholesterol, the high blood pressure and the diabetes hit you, you will remember these classes.

precepts.text: For we know that the law is spiritual; the statute for ever is understood in the spirit.
precepts.point: Christ told the disciples the Comforter would teach them all things and bring all things to their remembrance. Unless the Spirit of the Lord deals with you, you will never understand the Bible or the laws; that is why there was such contention between Christ and the Pharisees, for the Spirit had not revealed to them who he was.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
Paul writes, “we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.” The meat offering, fine flour with oil and frankincense, a handful burnt for a sweet savour and the remainder eaten unleavened by Aaron and his sons, is a statute for ever in your generations, and a statute for ever is understood in the spirit.

To understand how a perpetual statute of sacrifice pointed to Christ, the Spirit of Christ had to dwell in you. Paul, who wrote that the law is spiritual, did not understand it himself until Christ touched him on the way to Damascus.

precepts.text: The law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.
precepts.point: Thou shalt do that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord: not by personal standards of what feels good in the heart, but by the standard set before us, for the scripture says plainly that the law is good. The reward is to go in and possess the good land, the real wealth, not the bags and rings and sneakers, which are vanity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 6: Teach Them Diligently unto Thy Children

precepts.why:
“Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” The scripture says plainly that the law is good.

So doing “that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord” is doing the law, not what feels good in the heart. Paul and Moses agree: the commandment is holy, just and good, and diligently keeping it is what it means to do right and good, with the good land as the reward.

precepts.text: The law has dominion over a man as long as he lives, so as long as we are alive on this earth the law is not done away with.
precepts.point: I will walk at liberty, for I seek Thy precepts. I will speak of Thy testimonies also before kings and will not be ashamed, because we have the wisdom of this Bible, not the wisdom of this world.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Know ye not, brethren, (for I speak to them that know the law,) how that the law hath dominion over a man as long as he liveth?”

As long as we have breath the law has dominion over us; it is not done away with. That is why the psalm says “So shall I keep thy law continually for ever and ever”, and why we can walk at liberty seeking his precepts and speak of his testimonies before kings and not be ashamed, because we have the wisdom of this Bible, not the wisdom of this world.

precepts.text: Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good; the commandments are good for us.
precepts.point: For my brethren and companions' sakes, I will now say, Peace be within thee. My brethren are the twelve tribes. Because of the house of the Most High our God I will seek thy good, and the good is His law, His commandments, which are holy, just, and good for us.

note.label: Psalm 122: Pray for the Peace of Jerusalem

precepts.why: “Because of the house of the Lord our God I will seek thy good.” The good is his law, his commandments. “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” The commandments are good for us, and seeking Jerusalem’s good is seeking that law.

precepts.text: The law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good; the just are those seeking righteousness and keeping the commandments.
precepts.point: Therefore the prudent shall keep silence in that time, for it is an evil time.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

precepts.why:
“they afflict the just, they take a bribe, and they turn aside the poor in the gate from their right.” Who are the just? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” The just are those seeking righteousness and keeping the commandments.

So the manifold transgressions and mighty sins the Most High knows are against the ones keeping his law, and against the poor, whom they turn aside in the gate as though they do not even see them, which is not the spirit of Christ. Therefore the prudent keep silence in that time, for it is an evil time.

precepts.text: The law is holy, and the commandment holy, just, and good, so a just man is one who keeps the law.
precepts.point: Cornelius is now called a just man, adding to devout from verse 2, and to be just is to keep the law that is holy, just, and good. Even the southern kingdom, which had no dealings with the north, understood that this particular man of the northern tribes kept the commandments and had a good reputation, like Tobit before him, so they vouched for him by his pattern of good works and alms.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
The men told Peter, “Cornelius the centurion, a just man, and one that feareth God, and of good report among all the nation of the Jews.” Now Cornelius is called just, adding to devout from verse 2.

“Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” To be just is to keep the law that is holy, just and good. A just man is one who keeps the law.

Even the southern kingdom, which had no dealings with the north, understood that this particular man of the northern tribes kept the commandments and had a good reputation, like Tobit before him. So they vouched for him by his pattern of good works and alms.

precepts.point: Through the law of animal sacrifice, Paul is now dead to the law of animal sacrifice, that he might live unto God. Romans 7:4 confirms: 'ye also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ.' We are dead to the law of animal sacrifice by the body of Christ because Christ laid down his life for us.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Through the law of animal sacrifice, Paul is now dead to the law of animal sacrifice, that he might live unto God. Romans confirms: “Wherefore, my brethren, ye also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ; that ye should be married to another, even to him who is raised from the dead, that we should bring forth fruit unto God.”

We are dead to the law of animal sacrifice by the body of Christ, because Christ laid down his life for us. Being dead to that law, we are married to him who is raised from the dead and bring forth fruit unto God.

points: Sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me. Sin will deceive you. Brothers want to do right; I know you want to stop certain things. But why do you still go back and do it? Because sin deceives you. If this whole society is built on sin and you are around it all the time, it will deceive you. In the beginning God took the righteous away so the wickedness would not corrupt them; it is the same thing today. This society is very evil and wicked, and if all you see every day is certain things, it will affect you.

note.label: Sexual Discipline

points: Paul says, I was alive without the law once: that is when he was under the old covenant. But when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died. And the commandment, which was ordained to life, I found to be unto death.

Sin revived: when you come to serve God, after a while you say, I was not dealing with this before; where did this demon come from? Satan is trying to destroy you. Sin becomes harder to battle now because you are aware of it and you have changed your life; it is warfare.

note.label: Born for Adversity

points: For when we were in the flesh, the motions of sins did work in our members to bring forth fruit unto death: we did sinful things by nature, adultery, lying, stealing.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

points: But now we are delivered from the law, that we should serve in newness of spirit, and not in the oldness of the letter. The newness of spirit refers to the new covenant in Christ; the oldness of the letter refers to the covenant of animal sacrifice. When Paul talks about the law here, Christians think we are talking about sacrificing animals. If they took the time to listen and stop assuming, things would be all right.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

points: What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet. By reading and studying the law you know what sin is. This is why churches teach their members not to read Genesis to Malachi; they say start with Matthew, start in the middle of the book.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

points: I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind. This is Galatians 5:17. The mind is where the soul resides, and the flesh is trying to fight the soul, to bring me into captivity to the law of sin which is in my members.

Anybody who pretends that this fight is not present in them is not going to be able to endure in this walk. You have to acknowledge what your vices are, what your members are; you have members for good and members for sin. You have to own those things.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

points: O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death? From the day you are born, you are heading toward death, and the only thing on the other side is the preservation of your soul, which only God can do. Fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body, versus men who can only destroy the body.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

points: Sin, taking occasion by the commandment, wrought in me all manner of concupiscence. Wrought means it worked in me. Definition read in class: concupiscence is strong desire, especially sexual desire. Paul never said which kind he battled; he said all manner, and left it open. The point is that even Paul, doing the work, had evil thoughts warring in him.

note.label: They Say We Hate White People

points: When I would do good, evil is present with me. Even though Paul was doing the work, there was a reminder of the evil in him. He delighted in the law of God after the inward man, but saw another law in his members, warring against the law of his mind.

note.label: They Say We Hate White People

points: The law is spiritual, but I am carnal, sold under sin: carnal because I am in this carnal flesh. Paul is describing the mental battle: that which I do, I allow not; what I would, that do I not. Paul is not admitting himself to be in sin; he is telling you that mentally he is fighting against the flesh.

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

points: If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good. Every time you have an opportunity to sin and you choose God's word over sin, you are consenting that the law has been good the whole time. I could lie right now, but I am not going to, because the Bible says lie not one to another; I just consented that God's law is good. Every single time we refuse a sin, we are saying God is right and I am wrong.

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

points: I find then a law, that, when I would do good, evil is present with me: sin is always hovering, the old man trying to pull you back into wickedness. I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind: this body does not play fair.

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

points: So when somebody tells you that you cannot keep God's laws, that is a lie. They do not get up and murder people; they do not rob banks. Why not? Because they are consenting that God's law is good. Although we are in this carnal flesh, we prove daily that we can apply God's commandments to our life.

O wretched man that I am! Who shall deliver me from the body of this death? I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. With the mind I myself serve the law of God, but with the flesh the law of sin. This is the battle of every man and every woman on this earth. The difference between them and us is that we know why we battle it, and we have the keys to fix it.

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

points: I had not known sin, but by the law: the only way you know you are in sin against God is by referring back to his laws. When you read God's laws you say, he said do not do this; I have to change that. This is how you get the brain right.

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

points: Sin, taking occasion by the commandment, wrought in me all manner of concupiscence. Definition read in class: concupiscence is an intense longing or desire, a disordered human inclination or tendency to sin, stemming from selfish, worldly, or carnal appetites. That is the sinful nature, the shapen in iniquity.

note.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

points: If you do things you are not supposed to do, it is no more you that do it, but sin that dwelleth in you. I find then a law, that, when I would do good, evil is present with me: evil is present with all of us, all the time. When you want to do good, Satan is always there too, tempting you and trying to destroy you.

Somebody says something to you and it triggers things in your mind: who does that person think they are talking to? Some of these officers can be disrespectful sometimes, and when we find out you are rolling like that, we are going to take your rank. But even when a brother is wrong in how he dealt with you, you still cannot entertain them kind of evil thoughts, because them evil thoughts turn into bitterness. Everybody in here is trying to become perfect, and imperfect people will offend you; you either go to that person and fix it, or you cannot sit there and become bitter and hateful.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: I delight in the law of God after the inward man: the inward man is your mind, the inner you.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind: there is something in you that wars against your mind. You want to do good, you want to do right, but something is telling you evil stuff all the time. Them thoughts in your mind warring against your mind is Satan.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: And bringing me into captivity to the law of sin: that is what Satan is trying to do, bring you into the captivity of sin, the captivity of bitterness. O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death? I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord: so then with the mind I myself serve the law of God. Everything starts with your mind; when them evil thoughts come to your mind concerning your brother or your sister, you have to shake it off. Do not play with bitterness, hatred, or envy; when these things try creeping up in you, shake it off.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: The law is holy, just and good. Keeping it means keeping all of it, including the command against gluttony.
Keep my commandments and live. Whoever does not keep the law will not live.

note.label: My Temple My Choice

points: The law is spiritual, but I am carnal. The law reveals sin, and the more you study, the more your own lust and covetousness show themselves.
What I hate, that do I; it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me. The sin was already within and only manifested itself. Acknowledge it and turn away.
Husband and wife must keep talking. A wife who says her husband never spends time with her should make the time and set the table herself.
